title: The CAP theorem and eventual consistency

videos.script: The CAP theorem is usually quoted as pick two of three. That is not what it says. {{claim}} It says that when the network between two copies breaks, each request gets a stale answer or no answer. {{split}} In this lesson you break that network on purpose. With a synchronous replica, a sale waits. Five seconds, then the buyer gives up. {{sync}} And then, when the network comes back, the sale completes anyway. The buyer was told nothing, and has a ticket. {{timeout}} With an asynchronous replica, the sale goes through, and the page says the seat is still free for as long as the break lasts. {{async}} Then the everyday cost. Waiting for the replica made every commit almost a millisecond slower, on a healthy network. {{pacelc}} Last, two sides that both accepted writes. One rule loses a sale. Another keeps all of them, because of how the data is shaped. {{merge}}
